title: Formal or informal?
goal: Choose tu or vous in a written message, and open and close it with the right formula for a friend, a teacher or an organization.

items.en: keeping tu or vous consistent in a message

drills.text: Bonjour Madame Roy, est-ce que ___ pourriez m'envoyer le formulaire ?
drills.en: Hello Ms. Roy, could you send me the form?
drills.explain: Madame Roy is not a close friend: use vous, and keep it for the whole message.

drills.text: Salut Karim ! Tu peux m'envoyer ___ adresse ?
drills.en: Hi Karim! Can you send me your address?
drills.explain: With tu, the possessive is ton / ta / tes. Adresse starts with a vowel, so ton, not ta.

drills.prompt: You write to your landlord for the first time. Which sentence keeps the right register?
options: Pourriez-vous me rappeler, s'il vous plaît ?
Tu peux me rappeler, s'il te plaît ?
Pourriez-vous me rappeler, s'il te plaît ?
drills.explain: A landlord you don't know well gets vous, and s'il vous plaît goes with vous. Option 3 mixes the two.

items.en: Dear Sir or Madam, (formal opening, name unknown)

example.fr: Merci de votre aide. Cordialement, Raj Patel
example.en: Thank you for your help. Kind regards, Raj Patel

items.en: Hugs, (closing to a close friend or family)
items.note: Only for people you would greet with a kiss on the cheek or a hug.

items.en: Hope to see you again! (polite, friendly closing common in Québec)

items.note: Courriel is the usual word in Québec. In France you mostly hear un mail or un e-mail.

items.fr: Je vous remercie de votre réponse.
accept: Je vous remercie pour votre réponse.

steps.title: Same news, two messages
steps.intro: Amira's son Yanis was sick this week. On the same evening, she writes to her friend Lucie and to Yanis's teacher. Read both and notice what changes.

blocks.title: Message 1: to her friend Lucie
blocks.fr:
Salut Lucie !
Désolée, je ne peux pas venir à ton souper samedi. Yanis a été malade toute la semaine et il est encore fatigué. Tu veux venir prendre un café chez moi dimanche ? Je vais faire un gâteau !
Bises,
Amira
blocks.en: Hi Lucie! Sorry, I can't come to your supper on Saturday. Yanis has been sick all week and he's still tired. Do you want to come for a coffee at my place on Sunday? I'm going to make a cake! Hugs, Amira

blocks.title: Message 2: to Yanis's teacher
blocks.fr:
Objet : Absence de Yanis Benali, troisième année

Bonjour Madame Tremblay,

Mon fils Yanis n'est pas venu à l'école hier et avant-hier : il a eu de la fièvre. Il va mieux maintenant et il va revenir en classe demain matin.

Pourriez-vous me dire quels devoirs il doit faire ? Il peut les faire ce soir.

Merci d'avance et bonne journée.

Cordialement,
Amira Benali
blocks.en: Subject: Absence of Yanis Benali, grade 3. Hello Ms. Tremblay, My son Yanis didn't come to school yesterday or the day before: he had a fever. He's better now and he'll come back to class tomorrow morning. Could you tell me which homework he needs to do? He can do it tonight. Thanks in advance and have a good day. Kind regards, Amira Benali

blocks.prompt: Why does Amira write “Tu veux venir…” to Lucie but “Pourriez-vous me dire…” to the teacher?
options: Lucie is a close friend; the teacher is someone she knows only in a formal role
Lucie is younger than the teacher
blocks.explain: Register depends on the **relationship**: friends get **tu**; a teacher, a landlord or an office gets **vous**. Age alone is not the rule, and Madame Tremblay is a woman.

blocks.prompt: Which elements appear only in the message to the teacher?
options: A subject line, her full name and a professional closing
blocks.explain: A formal email has an [[Objet]] (subject line), a closing formula like [[Cordialement]] and your **full name**. Both messages have a greeting, a reason and a question.

blocks.prompt: Which closing would be strange in the message to Lucie?
blocks.explain: [[Salutations distinguées]] is very formal: for an official letter or a company. To a friend it sounds cold, almost like a joke.

blocks.title: Tu or vous in writing
blocks.body:
In writing, the choice is the same as in speech, but it shows more, because the reader keeps your message.

- **Tu**: friends, family, children, classmates, and colleagues who already use tu with you.
- **Vous**: people you don't know, your landlord, a teacher, a doctor's office, a company, an employer, older people you don't know well.

**When in doubt, use vous.** If the other person replies with tu, or writes [[On peut se tutoyer ?]] (Shall we use tu?), you can switch. Using vous with someone is called [[vouvoyer]]; using tu is [[tutoyer]].

blocks.title: Everything changes together
head: With tu
With vous
English
rows: Can you / Could you call me?
ton adresse, ta classe, tes devoirs
votre adresse, votre classe, vos devoirs
blocks.note: The classic slip is a **mix**: [[Bonjour Madame, tu peux…]] or [[Pourriez-vous… s'il te plaît ?]]. Choose once, then check every verb, pronoun and possessive.

blocks.title: Openings and closings by register
head: Informal (friend)
Polite (known person: teacher, colleague, landlord)
Formal (organization, unknown person)
rows: Je vous remercie de votre réponse.
Amira Benali (+ phone or file number)
blocks.note: Write [[Madame]] + **family name**, never + first name: [[Madame Tremblay]], not *Madame Julie*. When you don't know who will read the message (a company, an office), use [[Madame, Monsieur,]].

blocks.title: The shape of a polite email
blocks.pattern: Objet → Bonjour Madame X, → reason → details → request → thanks → closing → full name
blocks.note: Keep each part short. One idea per paragraph, and a blank line between paragraphs.

examples.fr: Je ne peux pas venir à mon rendez-vous de jeudi.
examples.en: I can't come to my appointment on Thursday.

examples.fr: Est-ce que je pourrais avoir un autre rendez-vous la semaine prochaine ?
examples.en: Could I have another appointment next week?

examples.fr: Je vous remercie. Cordialement, Mei Chen
examples.en: Thank you. Kind regards, Mei Chen

blocks.body:
- [[Cher Madame]] → [[Chère Madame]]: the adjective agrees. But [[Cher / Chère]] sounds personal; with someone you don't know, [[Bonjour Madame,]] or [[Madame,]] is safer.
- [[Salut Madame Tremblay]]: [[Salut]] is informal, so it clashes with [[Madame]]. Use [[Bonjour]].
- [[Madame Julie]]: use the family name, [[Madame Tremblay]], or just [[Bonjour Julie,]] if she signs with her first name.
- **Mixing tu and vous** in the same message: reread every verb and every [[ton / votre]].
- [[Cordialement]] to a friend sounds cold. [[Bises]] to your landlord is far too familiar.
- No closing at all in a formal email: always end with a formula and your full name.

blocks.title: Why so many closings?
blocks.body:
French writing marks the **distance** between people more clearly than English. Think of a scale:

[[Bises]] (very close) → [[À bientôt]] → [[Bonne journée]] → [[Cordialement]] (neutral, professional) → [[Bien à vous]] → [[Salutations distinguées]] (very formal).

In emails, [[Cordialement]] is the safe middle: you can use it with almost any office or company. In France, very formal paper letters end with a long sentence such as *Veuillez agréer, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées*. You only need to **recognize** it for now.

- In Québec, [[Bonjour]] + name is the normal opening for work emails, even to people you have never met: [[Bonjour Madame Gagnon,]] or simply [[Bonjour,]].
- Québec offices often close with [[Merci et bonne journée,]] or [[Au plaisir,]] (short for *au plaisir de vous revoir*, meaning *hope to hear from you again*).
- [[Salutations distinguées]] is still common in Québec for formal letters and complaints.
- The usual word is [[courriel]] (email). Many people also say [[un mail]] or [[un e-mail]] in France, and you will hear [[un message texte]] or [[un texto]] for a text message.
- Québec workplaces switch to **tu** quickly. Still start with **vous** with clients, government offices, older people and anyone in authority, and let them offer tu.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: These formulas are often read aloud in voicemails too. Say them smoothly, as one chunk.

lines.tip: Tremblay: the final -ay sounds like the è in mère.
Monsieur sounds like “muh-syuh”: the r is silent.

lines.fr: Je vous remercie de votre réponse.

lines.en: Thanks in advance and have a good day.

lines.tip: distinguées: the gu is a hard g, like in “go”.

lines.fr: Pourriez-vous me rappeler, s'il vous plaît ?
lines.en: Could you call me back, please?

blocks.fr: Bonjour Monsieur Gagnon, c'est Raj Patel, de l'appartement 3. Pourriez-vous me rappeler, s'il vous plaît ? Merci et bonne journée.
blocks.en: Hello Mr. Gagnon, it's Raj Patel, from apartment 3. Could you call me back, please? Thanks and have a good day.
blocks.prompt: Raj leaves a voicemail. Who is he probably talking to?
options: His landlord, someone he doesn't know well
A close friend from his French class
blocks.explain: [[Monsieur Gagnon]], [[Pourriez-vous]], [[s'il vous plaît]] and [[de l'appartement 3]]: all polite vous forms, typical with a landlord.

blocks.fr: Coucou Mei ! Tu viens au parc avec nous cet après-midi ? Réponds-moi vite ! Bisous !
blocks.en: Hey Mei! Are you coming to the park with us this afternoon? Answer me quickly! Kisses!
blocks.prompt: What is the relationship between the speaker and Mei?
blocks.explain: [[Coucou]], [[tu]], [[réponds-moi]] (the tu imperative) and [[Bisous]] are all informal: this is a friend or a family member.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Choose the register first, then the words. Answer without scrolling back.

blocks.prompt: You email your new landlord, Marc Gagnon, for the first time. Which opening is best?
optionFeedback: Salut is informal and clashes with Monsieur.
Coucou is for friends and family.
Cher + first name is personal: fine for a friend, not for a landlord you don't know.

blocks.prompt: You write to a company's customer service. You don't know who will read it. How do you open?
blocks.explain: [[Madame, Monsieur,]] is the standard opening when the reader is unknown. With a family name, never a first name, after [[Madame]].

blocks.text: Bonjour Madame Roy, vous pouvez m'envoyer ___ adresse, s'il vous plaît ?
blocks.en: Hello Ms. Roy, can you send me your address, please?
blocks.explain: With vous, the possessive is [[votre]] (one thing) or [[vos]] (several). [[Adresse]] is singular: [[votre adresse]].

blocks.prompt: Thank you for your reply. (formal email)
accept: Je vous remercie de votre réponse.
Je vous remercie pour votre réponse.
blocks.explain: [[Je vous remercie de / pour…]] is the most formal; [[Merci pour votre réponse]] is also fine. Keep [[votre]], not [[ta]].

blocks.prompt: Match each closing with when you use it.
pairs: only for close friends and family
friendly, also fine with a colleague you know
polite and friendly, common in Québec

blocks.en: Dear Ms. Lavoie, (to a neighbour you know well)
blocks.explain: [[Cher]] agrees with the person: [[Chère Madame]], [[Cher Monsieur]]. It's warm, so keep it for people you know.

blocks.prompt: Could you send me the documents? (formal)
blocks.explain: [[Pourriez-vous]] + infinitive is a very polite request. The pronoun [[m']] goes right before the infinitive.
[[S'il te plaît]] shows you use tu, so the imperative is the tu form: [[réponds-moi]]. With vous it would be [[répondez-moi]].

accept: Mon fils a été malade hier.
Hier, mon fils a été malade.
blocks.explain: A finished episode: [[a été malade]] (passé composé). [[Était malade]] (imparfait) is also possible when you describe the state.
[[d'avance]] = in advance: de + avance, with an apostrophe.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.intro: Same news, two readers. That is the whole skill of this lesson.

blocks.prompt: You are sick and can't come to your French class tomorrow. Write two short messages (60–100 words in total): one text to a classmate who is a friend (tu), and one email to your teacher, Madame Roy (vous). Say what happened, ask for the homework, and close each message correctly.
blocks.promptFr: Vous êtes malade. Écrivez à un ami de la classe, puis à votre professeure, Madame Roy.
checklist: Message 1: Salut + name, tu forms, a friendly closing (Bises / À bientôt)
Message 2: Objet, Bonjour Madame Roy, vous forms throughout
What happened, in the passé composé: j'ai eu de la fièvre / je suis allé chez le médecin
A request: Tu peux m'envoyer… ? / Pourriez-vous m'envoyer… ?
Thanks and a correct closing: Merci d'avance. Cordialement, + full name
Final check: no mix of tu and vous inside one message

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
Salut Sofia ! Je suis malade, je ne viens pas au cours demain. Tu peux m'envoyer les devoirs ? Merci ! À bientôt, Nguyen

Objet : Absence au cours de demain
Bonjour Madame Roy,
Je suis malade depuis hier : j'ai eu de la fièvre toute la nuit. Je ne peux pas venir au cours demain. Pourriez-vous m'envoyer les devoirs ?
Merci d'avance.
Cordialement,
Nguyen Van Minh
models.en: Hi Sofia! I'm sick, I'm not coming to class tomorrow. Can you send me the homework? Thanks! See you soon, Nguyen. Subject: Absence from tomorrow's class. Hello Ms. Roy, I've been sick since yesterday: I had a fever all night. I can't come to class tomorrow. Could you send me the homework? Thanks in advance. Kind regards, Nguyen Van Minh

models.label: Stronger model answer
models.fr:
Coucou Sofia ! Mauvaise nouvelle : j'ai attrapé la grippe et je reste au lit. Je ne serai pas au cours demain. Tu pourrais m'envoyer une photo de tes notes ? Je te remercie ! Bises, Lucie

Objet : Absence le jeudi 14 mars
Bonjour Madame Roy,
Je vous écris pour vous dire que je ne pourrai pas venir au cours demain : je suis allée chez le médecin ce matin et j'ai la grippe. Pourriez-vous me dire quels exercices je dois faire ? Je vais les faire à la maison.
Je vous remercie de votre compréhension.
Cordialement,
Lucie Martin
models.en: Hey Sofia! Bad news: I caught the flu and I'm staying in bed. I won't be in class tomorrow. Could you send me a photo of your notes? Thank you! Hugs, Lucie. Subject: Absence on Thursday, March 14. Hello Ms. Roy, I'm writing to tell you that I won't be able to come to class tomorrow: I went to the doctor this morning and I have the flu. Could you tell me which exercises I need to do? I'll do them at home. Thank you for your understanding. Kind regards, Lucie Martin

blocks.prompt: Leave a short voicemail for Madame Roy's school office (25 seconds): greet politely, say who you are, say you are sick and can't come tomorrow, ask them to tell Madame Roy, and close politely.
blocks.promptFr: Laissez un message au secrétariat de l'école.
checklist: C'est + your full name, de la classe de Madame Roy
Je suis malade, je ne peux pas venir demain.
Pourriez-vous le dire à Madame Roy ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour, madame. C'est Karim Haddad, de la classe de Madame Roy. Je suis malade depuis hier et je ne peux pas venir au cours demain. Pourriez-vous le dire à Madame Roy, s'il vous plaît ? Merci et bonne journée !
models.en: Hello, madam. It's Karim Haddad, from Ms. Roy's class. I've been sick since yesterday and I can't come to class tomorrow. Could you tell Ms. Roy, please? Thanks and have a good day!

summary:
- Choose **tu** or **vous** for each reader, and keep it consistent: verbs, pronouns, possessives, imperatives
- Open with [[Salut !]], [[Bonjour Madame Tremblay,]] or [[Madame, Monsieur,]]
- Close with [[Bises]], [[À bientôt]], [[Cordialement]], [[Bien à vous]] or [[Salutations distinguées]], and sign with your full name in formal emails
